info.title: Studio API
info.description:
Studio turns audio and video into transcriptions, translations, subtitles and dubbing. Use this API to create projects, order translation and dubbing, follow the progress, and download the results.

## Authentication
Send your Phrase Platform API token with every request, as `X-API-Key: <token>` or as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, invalid or expired token is answered with `401`. `403` means the token is valid but the action is not allowed: the item is someone else's, a share does not include the step or language, or your organization is blocked.

## Typical flow
1. Create a project with `POST /v1/projects`: upload files, or give direct links to media files. It answers with the project `id`. To add a recording to a project that exists, call `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/upload-url`, upload the file to the url it returns, then call `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings`.
2. Poll `GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/{recordingId}/status` until the transcription is `done`. Every long step answers `202` and runs in the background: you poll the status, you do not wait on the call.
3. Optional: `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/{recordingId}/estimates` tells what a translation costs before you start it.
4. Order translation with `POST …/translate`, and wait until the status shows the language as `done`.
5. Order dubbing with `POST …/dubbing`. A language must be translated before it can be dubbed, otherwise the call answers `400`.
6. Read and download: `GET …/subtitles` for the text, the result endpoints for summary and insights, `POST …/exports` for a file, then `GET …/exports/{exportId}` until it is `done`.

## Credits
Credits are minutes. Transcription and every new translation language use `ceil(duration / 60)` minutes of the recording. Dubbing, retranscription and retranslation use none. The estimate endpoint tells the price in advance. When an organization has no credits left, starting work is refused with `403` (`No remaining minutes available`): creating a project, adding a recording, transcribe, translate, dubbing, sync-dubbing and speech. Reading results, estimates and editing the text of subtitles still work. The same goes for a re-dub (`PUT .../subtitles` with `segmentsToRedub`), re-syncing a dubbing and generating speech with `POST /v1/tts/speech`: they make new speech, so a blocked organization is refused for them too.

## Errors
Errors are JSON: `{ "statusCode": 400, "message": "...", "timestamp": "..." }`. The `message` says what to change.
- `400` the request is invalid.
- `401` the token is missing, invalid or expired.
- `403` the token is valid but the action is not allowed: your share of a project does not include the step or language, the project does not exist or is not shared with you (project routes do not tell the two apart), or your organization has no credits left for an action that needs them.
- `404` the item does not exist, or you may not manage it: a recording that is not in the project, or a glossary, template, insight, pronunciation set, subtitle profile, font or voice of your organization that does not exist. Settings of another organization answer `404` too.
- `409` the request conflicts with what exists: a name that is taken, a recording that was added already, a speaker that is still in use, or a template that a trigger still uses. The message says which.
- `429` too many requests; wait and try again.
- `5xx` a failure on our side or at a provider; try again later.

## Where the ids come from
Ids that Studio accepts but does not list belong to other Phrase products. `tmsProjectTemplateUid`, `termBases`, `mtProfileId` and `translationMemoryId` are Phrase TMS uids: get them from the Phrase TMS API (project templates, term bases, translation memories, machine translation profiles). `styleGuides` ids come from the Style Guides API. Both are described at https://developers.phrase.com/en/api/overview. Every other id (projects, recordings, glossaries, insights, pronunciations, templates, subtitle profiles, voices) comes from the list endpoints of this API.

post.description:
Creates an empty project and redirects the client to the upload service to upload files. After upload completion, the service will finalize the project automatically. Upload files with the `files` parts of the request. `fileUrls` also works for direct links to media files: an `https://` link that anyone can download and that ends in an audio or video file, not a web page. Uploading files is more robust than links.

This endpoint does not accept translation or dubbing languages — a project is created transcription-only. Once transcription completes, call `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/{recordingId}/translate` to add translation languages, then `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/{recordingId}/dubbing` to add dubbing languages.

Upload behavior and limits:
- 10-minute inactivity timeout per upload stream.
- If the client connection drops, the upload is aborted and cannot resume; retry from the start.
- Multi-hour uploads are supported as long as data keeps flowing and the connection stays open.

Supported sources: files you upload and direct links to audio or video files. The file is checked after it is downloaded: if it has no audio or video stream the request is rejected with `400` and no project is created.

Errors of the upload, as `{ success, statusCode, message }`:
- `400` `The file at the URL is not an audio or video file`: the link points to a web page or another kind of file.
- `400` `The URL could not be downloaded: the server answered <status>`: the server of the link refused, for example with `404` or `403`.
- `400` `Invalid fileUrls entry: ...`: the link is not an `https://` URL or points to a host that is not allowed.
- `400` `Unsupported file type. Allowed: mp4, mov, mp3, wav, m4a`: a file part of another type.
- `400` `Invalid JSON in: <fields>`: `expectedLanguages`, `insights`, `glossary`, `safeCommunications`, `pronunciations` or `fileUrls` is not valid JSON.
- `400` `The recording is longer than 180 minutes`: a recording may be at most 180 minutes long.
- `400` `Maximum 50 files allowed`: a project takes at most 50 files, uploads and links together.
- `413` a file is larger than 20 GB.
- `502` the server of the link failed or could not be reached, or the project could not be started.

Credits: the transcription of every recording uses `ceil(duration / 60)` minutes. A project whose organization has no credits left is refused with `403`.

patch.description:
Update the settings of a project: the models for translation and insights, the machine translation profile and translation memory, the text-to-speech engine, and the sharing visibility. Which of the machine translation profile and the translation memory apply depends on the translation model, as in Studio: `plai` (Phrase Language AI) takes both, chosen by you; `aita` (AI Translation Agent) takes a translation memory, and Studio chooses its machine translation profile; `gpt-5-mini` and `gpt-4o-mini` take neither. Changing the model keeps the settings that still apply and clears the ones that do not; sending a setting that does not apply is refused with `400`. For `aita` Studio looks up the machine translation profile in your Phrase TMS connection and answers `400` when there is none. The model types follow from the models and are not sent. The endpoint is partial: only fields present in the body are written, so a single field can be changed without resending the rest. Authorization is restricted to the project owner and other accounts in the same organization.

The same call renames the project with `name`. Updating the settings or renaming is for the owner of the project and managers of the organization; for anyone else the answer is `404`.

get.description:
Poll how far the processing of a recording is: transcription, each translation language, each dubbing language and the summary, with the reason when a step failed.

This is the URL returned as `statusUrl` by the translate and dubbing endpoints.

## Reading the result

- `status` is the overall state. Poll until it is `done` or `failed`.
- Each step has its own `status`. A `failed` step carries `errorCode` and `errorMessage`; on every other state both are `null`.
- A translation that runs through a translation management job also carries `tmsJob`. It stays `pending` until that job delivers.
- A step that was requested but not started yet is listed as `pending`.

## Shared projects

If your share of the project is limited to some languages, only those translation and dubbing languages are listed and the overall `status` is computed from what you can see.

put.description:
Replace the subtitle segments of a recording's language track. The request body must contain **every** segment in the final state — the endpoint performs a bulk replace, not a partial patch. Any segment you omit is removed from the track. Use this to push subtitle edits made externally (for example, by AI editing tools) back into Studio.

## `words` is the source of truth — never send empty `words`

Each segment's `words` array (word-level text and timings) is authoritative. Subtitle rendering **and** dubbing text-to-speech are generated from `words`; the segment-level `text` field is only a human-readable mirror and is **ignored** when rendering subtitles or synthesizing speech.

A segment whose `words` array is empty is treated as having no content: it is **silently dropped the next time the track is read**, and for dubbing nothing is synthesized for it. This is the most common cause of a track that “comes back empty” after an update. Never submit `"words": []` unless you intend to remove that segment's content.

To change what a segment says — for example, shortening a dubbing line — rewrite its `words` array, not just `text`. Mirror the change in `text` for readability, but the `words` entries are what actually change the rendered subtitle and the generated audio.

## Recommended workflow

1. `GET` the track to fetch the current segments with their word-level timings.
2. Edit the `words` array of the segment(s) you want to change (and mirror the new text in `text`). Leave every other segment untouched.
3. `PUT` the **full** segment array back. For a dubbing redub, list the changed segment ids in `segmentsToRedub` and keep `enqueueTtsUpdate=true` so their audio is regenerated from the new `words`.

To edit text without triggering re-synthesis, set `enqueueTtsUpdate` to `false` — but still send the full `words` array for every segment.

## Position, styling and comments

Each segment can carry what the Studio editor offers, and the same fields are returned by `GET` and accepted by `PUT`:

* **Position** — `cue_settings` (see `CueSettings`).
* **Style** — `style` (see `SubtitleStyle`): font, size, colors, background and position of this segment's subtitle, overriding the subtitle profile.
* **Word styles** — `<b>`, `<i>` and `<u>` tags inside `words[].word`.
* **Review state** — `metadata.review` (`status`, `reviewedBy`, `reviewedAt`).
* **Per-segment dubbing settings** — `metadata.dubbing` (`volume`, `stability`, `similarity`, `needsRedub`). The audio durations it also returns are read-only and ignored on `PUT`.
* **Comments** — `comments`. A segment that sends no `comments` keeps the comments stored in Studio; an array replaces them (comments missing from it are deleted) and an empty array deletes all of them.
* **On-screen text** — text detected in the video is returned as ordinary segments with `speaker` set to `On Screen Text` and `metadata.onScreenText` set to `true`. They carry a `cue_settings` position, are never dubbed and may overlap each other (and the spoken segments) in time. Send them back unchanged with the rest of the track; a `PUT` that leaves them out removes them. Assigning a segment to the `On Screen Text` speaker and setting `metadata.onScreenText` makes it on-screen text.

Because `PUT` replaces the whole track, send back the `cue_settings`, `style` and `comments` you got from `GET` for the segments you did not change.

Versions saved with an API key are listed as **API** in Studio's Version History; the author is not taken from the request body.

## Language scoping

The `language` value must match the requested task type for the recording:
* When `source=true` and `dubbing=false` (transcription), `language` must equal the recording source language.
* When `source=false` and `dubbing=false` (translation), `language` must be one of the recording translation languages.
* When `source=false` and `dubbing=true` (dubbing), `language` must be one of the recording translation languages.
* `source=true` and `dubbing=true` together is invalid.

Mismatched combinations return `400` with a descriptive message rather than reaching the underlying file lookup.

## Review state and QA warnings

**Review state.** `metadata.review` holds `status` (`PENDING` or `REVIEWED`), `reviewedBy` and `reviewedAt`, per segment, on every track. To mark a segment as reviewed, `GET` the track, set `metadata.review` to `{ "status": "REVIEWED", "reviewedBy": { "id": "<uuid>", "name": "<name>" }, "reviewedAt": "<ISO date-time>" }` on that segment and `PUT` the full track back. The server stores the review exactly as sent and does not verify the reviewer. It does **not** change the review when you change the text of a segment: the Studio editor sets a segment back to `PENDING` when a person edits it, but this endpoint stores what you send, so set `PENDING` yourself on every segment whose text you rewrite. A segment sent without `metadata.review` counts as not reviewed.

**Review progress.** `reviewProgress` on `GET /v1/projects` and on `GET /v1/projects/{id}` counts `reviewedSegments` against `totalSegments` for each step and language, recomputed from the segments of every track on each `PUT`. A shared project only lists the steps and languages its share includes.

**QA warnings.** QA warnings are not stored or returned by the API. Studio computes them per segment from the rules of the project's subtitle profile (`GET /v1/subtitle-profiles`), and a caller can do the same. A segment breaks a rule when:

* its longest line has more than `maxLineCharacterCount` characters;
* its characters per second (characters of the text divided by its duration) is above `charactersPerSecond`;
* its duration is below `minDuration`, or below `minGapFrames` frames at the frame rate of the recording (`fps`);
* its duration is above `maxDuration`;
* it has more than `maxLinesPerScreen` lines;
* two consecutive words are further apart than `maxGapBetweenWords` seconds.

## What is checked

The same checks as in the Studio editor, in Studio and in this API:

* The track: `source=true` takes the source language of the recording; a translation track takes any language but the source language, also one the recording does not have yet (save its subtitles first, then call `POST .../translate` with it in `ignoredLanguages`, which adds the language and charges it); a dubbing track (`dubbing=true`) needs a language that is translated already. `source` and `dubbing` cannot both be `true`.
* A segment is at least 0.3 seconds long.
* Two segments of one speaker do not overlap. On-screen texts are left out of this: they may overlap each other and the spoken segments.

What is stored already is not held against you: a segment that is sent back exactly as it was stored (same id, same start and end) is accepted even when it is shorter than 0.3 seconds or overlaps another stored segment, so a recording whose transcription made such a segment can still be saved after you edit another one. A segment that you change, or a new one, has to pass. Anything refused answers `400` with the segment and the reason, and nothing is saved.

## Limits

At most 20,000 segments in one save, at most 2,500 words in a segment, a segment text of at most 5,000 characters, a word of at most 500 characters, and at most 200 speakers in `speakerVolumes` and `speakerVoiceSettings`. A request over a limit answers `400` and nothing is saved.

## Credits

Saving the text uses no credits. A save with `segmentsToRedub` and `enqueueTtsUpdate` makes new speech: an organization that has used up its credits (`balance.state` is `BLOCKED`) is refused with `403` for it.

post.description:
Add one or more target translation languages to a recording that already exists, without recreating the project. Use this instead of `POST /v1/projects` whenever the project already exists — for example the caller forgot a language at creation time, the user asks for another language later, or the caller only learns which language is needed after seeing the transcript.

## Precondition: source transcription must be complete

Translation reads the recording's transcript, so it can only run after transcription has finished. This is **not enforced synchronously** by this endpoint — a call made too early is accepted and queued, but produces no usable result. Before calling this endpoint, poll `GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/{recordingId}/status` until `transcription.status` is `done`.

## Re-requesting a language

A language already in the recording's translation languages is not skipped — it is retranslated (logged as a retranslation rather than an initial translation). Only include a language in `languages` if you actually want it (re-)translated. Use `ignoredLanguages` for a language whose subtitles you provide yourself: Studio does not translate it.

## Credits

Only a language the recording does not have yet is charged: `ceil(duration / 60)` minutes per language, also when you provide its subtitles yourself with `ignoredLanguages`. Retranslating a language the recording already has is free. `POST .../estimates` tells the price before you start. An organization that has used up its credits (`balance.state` is `BLOCKED`) is refused with `403` for every translation, charged or not

## Language support

`languages` accepts any BCP-47-style code Phrase Studio has translation support for — effectively all locales except the literal `auto` placeholder. Do not pass the recording's own source language: it is rejected with `400` (see `source_language_as_target` below), like an unsupported code. Nothing is started for any language of a rejected request.

## After translation completes

Call `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings/{recordingId}/dubbing` to dub any of the resulting languages — dubbing requires the language to be translated first.

## Response

The call answers `202 Accepted` as soon as the work is queued, not when it is done. The body's `statusUrl` is the path to poll (`GET`, same credentials) until the result you need is ready. If the work could not be started, the step is listed as `failed` with `errorCode` and `errorMessage` instead of the call failing.

name.description: New project name, at least 3 characters. Only the owner or an organization manager may rename.

translationModelName.description: Model that translates. `aita` is the AI Translation Agent (best quality), `plai` is Phrase Language AI, the two GPT models are the fast ones. Which of the machine translation profile and the translation memory apply depends on the translation model, as in Studio: `plai` (Phrase Language AI) takes both, chosen by you; `aita` (AI Translation Agent) takes a translation memory, and Studio chooses its machine translation profile; `gpt-5-mini` and `gpt-4o-mini` take neither. ttsProvider.description: Text-to-speech provider for dubbing. Some engines are switched on or off per organization: `GET /v1/tts/engines` lists the ones you can use, and an engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

Sending it for any other model is refused with `400`.

translationMemoryId.description: Phrase TMS translation memory uid, for the translation models `plai` and `aita`. Get it from the Phrase TMS API (translation memories); Studio has no endpoint that lists it. An empty string is refused with `400`. Changing to a GPT model removes it; setting it while the model is a GPT model is refused with `400`.

words.description: Word-level text and timings. **Source of truth** for both subtitle rendering and dubbing text-to-speech. Must be non-empty: a segment submitted with an empty `words` array is dropped the next time the track is read (and produces no dubbing audio). To change a segment's content, edit these entries — not `text`. **Inline styling:** put `…`, `…` or `…` around text inside `word` to make it bold, italic or underlined, for example `really`. A style that spans several words opens in the first word and closes in the last. Keep the tags balanced within a segment and do not change `time_begin` or `time_end` when you only add or remove a style. The tags stay in SRT and VTT exports and are rendered in burned-in subtitles; they are removed for dubbing and for plain-text exports. At most 2,500 words per segment, and at most 5,000 characters in the words together.

language.description: BCP-47 language code for the segment

text.description: Human-readable mirror of the segment text. **Not authoritative** — it is ignored when rendering subtitles or synthesizing dubbing audio, both of which are derived from `words`. Editing `text` alone has no effect on the output; change `words` instead (and keep `text` in sync for readability). At most 5,000 characters.

comments.description: Reviewer comments of the segment (at most 200). **Omit the field to keep the comments stored in Studio** for this segment. Send an array to replace them: a comment that is not in the array is deleted, and an empty array deletes all of them. To add a comment, send the current ones plus the new one; to resolve one, send it with `resolved: true`. Comments belong to subtitle tracks (source and translation), not to dubbing tracks.

Do not pass the recording's source language: the request is rejected with `400`, and nothing is started for any of its languages.

Studio's burn-in and the editor preview place the top of the subtitle box at `line` and the edge picked by `align` at `position`; vertical subtitle profiles ignore the position. displaySpeakerNames.description: Whether the speaker name is shown in front of the text.

maxLinesPerScreen.description: Maximum number of lines shown at the same time.

charactersPerSecond.description: Maximum reading speed in characters per second.

fontFamily.description: Font family: a name of 1-128 characters without commas, braces, backslashes or line breaks (such as `Arial`), or `custom:<id>` for a custom font (the `fontFamily` value of `GET /v1/fonts`) that you can use. A custom font that does not exist or is not yours is refused with `400`. A custom font that was deleted later falls back to Arial in burned-in video.

textColor.description: Text color: `#RRGGBB`, or `rgb()`/`rgba()` with channels 0-255 and an alpha from 0 to 1 (for example `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`); `backgroundColor` and `textColor` may also be empty.

backgroundType.description: How the text is separated from the video.

backgroundColor.description: Background color: `#RRGGBB`, or `rgb()`/`rgba()` with channels 0-255 and an alpha from 0 to 1 (for example `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`); `backgroundColor` and `textColor` may also be empty.

verticalPositioning.description: Whether subtitles are positioned vertically from the edge instead of by the placement setting.

TemplateSettings.description: What a project created from the template starts with.

expectedLanguages.description: Other languages that may be spoken.

isPublic.description: Whether the project is visible to the organization.

preferences.description: Project preferences such as the models and the text-to-speech provider.

insightsModelType.description: AI model provider type for insights.

translationModelType.description: AI model provider type for translation.

mtProfileId.description: Phrase TMS machine translation profile uid. Get it from the Phrase TMS API (machine translate profiles); Studio has no endpoint that lists it.

translationMemoryId.description: Phrase TMS translation memory uid. Get it from the Phrase TMS API (translation memories); Studio has no endpoint that lists it.

ttsProvider.description: Text-to-speech provider for dubbing. Some engines are switched on or off per organization: `GET /v1/tts/engines` lists the ones you can use, and an engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

tmsProjectTemplateUid.description: Phrase TMS project template uid. Get it from the Phrase TMS API (project templates); Studio has no endpoint that lists it.

subtitleProfiles.description: Subtitle profile ids by language code; an id that is not a UUID is refused with `400`.

styleGuides.description: Style guide ids by language code. Get them from the Style Guides API; Studio has no endpoint that lists them.

termBases.description: Phrase TMS term base uids by language code. Get them from the Phrase TMS API (term bases); Studio has no endpoint that lists them.

dubbing.description: Dubbing settings. Every dubbing language must also be a translation language or the source language.

pronunciations.description: Pronunciation set ids by language code; an id that is not a UUID is refused with `400`.

Template.description: A saved set of project settings that a new project can start from. Templates are shared with your organization.

UpdateTemplateRequest.description: Fields of a template to change. Send only what changes. `settings` replaces all settings.

VoiceClone.description: A saved voice of your organization ("My voices") that can be applied to the speaker of a recording.

id.description: Voice ID. Use it as `voiceId` when assigning the voice to a speaker. A voice with `source` `external` comes from the ElevenLabs account your organization connected: its ID is the ElevenLabs voice ID, not a UUID, and it can be listed and assigned to a speaker but not fetched, renamed or deleted here.

projectId.description: Project the voice was made from, if any.

source.description: How the voice was made, for example from an upload or from a recording.

previewUrl.description: Short link to a sample of the voice.

UpdateVoiceCloneRequest.description: Fields of a voice to change. Send only what changes.

name.description: Voice name, unique in your organization.

projectId.description: Project to relate the voice to. `null` removes the relation.

RecordingSpeaker.description: A speaker of a recording and the voices assigned to it.

speakerName.description: Speaker name as used in the subtitles.

providerVoices.description: Assigned voice per provider and language: `{ provider: { languageCode: voice } }`.

deletable.description: Whether the speaker can be removed without leaving the recording without a speaker.

payload.description: One entry per speaker and language.

speakerName.description: Speaker to assign the voice to. A name that does not exist yet creates the speaker.

language.description: Dubbing language the voice is used for.

voiceId.description: A voice `id` from `GET /v1/voices/clones`, or a voice id of the provider.

provider.description: Text-to-speech provider the voice is for. Defaults to the default provider of Studio. Some engines are switched on or off per organization: `GET /v1/tts/engines` lists the ones you can use, and an engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

ExternalTextExport.description: A subtitle or transcript file as text.

content.description: The whole file. Speaker names are included when the subtitle profile of the language shows them.

CreateExportRequest.description: What to export. `type` decides which other fields are needed; a request that lacks one is refused with `400`.

type.description: `burned_in_video`: the original video with the subtitles of `language` burned in (needs `language`). `dubbed_video`: the video with the dubbing of `dubbingLanguage`, optionally with `subtitleLanguage` burned in. `dubbed_videos`: one dubbed video per entry of `languages`, up to 5. `dubbed_audio`: the mixed dubbed audio of `dubbingLanguage`. `dubbed_audio_stems`: the dubbed speech and the background as separate files. `dubbed_audio_by_speaker`: one dubbed audio file per speaker. `source_audio`: the audio of the original recording. `bilingual_docx`: a Word document with the source text next to its translation (needs `language`, the translation language; `includeTimecode` adds a time column). It is made on the spot, so it answers `200` with its link.

language.description: Subtitle language: the language to burn in for `burned_in_video`, the translation language for `bilingual_docx`.

source.description: Use the source-language subtitles (the transcript) instead of the translation.

dubbing.description: Use the subtitles of the dubbing track instead of the translation. For `burned_in_video`.

dubbingLanguage.description: Language of the dubbing. For `dubbed_video`, `dubbed_audio`, `dubbed_audio_stems` and `dubbed_audio_by_speaker`.

subtitleLanguage.description: Subtitle language to burn into a dubbed video. Optional.

includeTimecode.description: Add a time column to the document. For `bilingual_docx`.

Export.description: An export of a recording: either ready, with its download link, or running, with the url to poll.

exportId.description: Identifies a running export. Absent when the export was ready at once.

type.description: The type that was requested. Present in the answer to the request.

status.description: `pending`: queued. `in_progress`: being rendered. `done`: ready, see `downloadUrl`. `failed`: stopped, see `errorMessage`.

downloadUrl.description: Signed link to the file, valid for three hours. Only when `status` is `done`.

statusUrl.description: Path to poll with `GET` and the same credentials until `status` is `done` or `failed`.

errorMessage.description: Why the export failed. Only when `status` is `failed`.

SourceFiles.description: The original file of a recording and its audio tracks.

sourceFileUrl.description: Signed link to the original file, valid for three hours.

audioTracks.description: Audio tracks of the recording: the original and one dubbed track per dubbed language.

language.description: Language of the track; `source_language` for the original.

kind.description: Whether it is the original audio or a dubbing.

url.description: Signed link to the audio, valid for three hours.

waveform.description: Signed link to the waveform data, valid for three hours.

SegmentAudio.description: The dubbed audio of the segments in a time range.

url.description: Signed link to the audio of the segment.

backgroundAudioUrl.description: Signed link to the background audio.

backgroundWaveformUrl.description: Signed link to the waveform of the background audio.

useNewDubbing.description: True when the dubbing supports the segment audio edits.

RecordingSummary.description: The summary Studio made of a recording.

CustomAttribute.description: A tag Studio found in a recording.

SafeCommunicationResult.description: The outcome of a safe communication check on a recording.

InsightResult.description: The answer to one item of an insight, for a recording.

SummarizeRecordingRequest.description: What to summarize. Send only what you want added.

safeCommunications.description: Safe communication IDs to check, from `GET /v1/safe-communications`.

TranscribeRecordingRequest.description: Settings for transcribing the recording again.

ignored.description: Skip transcription and keep the recording as it is.

expectedLanguages.description: Other languages that may be spoken.

subtitleProfiles.description: Subtitle profile id by language code.

SegmentAudioSpeedRequest.description: A new duration for the dubbed audio of one segment.

ttsDuration.description: New duration of the audio in seconds. Shorter is faster speech.

originalTtsDuration.description: Duration of the audio before any speed change, in seconds. Read it from `metadata.dubbing.originalTtsDuration` of the dubbing subtitles.

reset.description: Restore the original speed. Send `originalTtsDuration` as `ttsDuration` with it.

segmentStart.description: Start of the segment in seconds.

segmentEnd.description: End of the segment in seconds.

SegmentAudioSpeedResponse.description: The segment whose audio was changed.

url.description: Signed link to the new audio.

SegmentAudioSplitRequest.description: Split the dubbed audio of one segment in two.

newSegmentId.description: ID of the new second part.

duration.description: Duration of the new part in seconds.

SegmentAudioMergeRequest.description: Merge the dubbed audio of two segments.

survivingSegmentId.description: Segment that keeps the merged audio.

removedSegmentId.description: Segment whose audio is merged into it and removed.

gapDuration.description: Silence between the two in seconds.

BackgroundAudioUpload.description: A new background audio for a dubbing language.

language.description: Dubbing language the background is for.

file.description: The audio file: MP3, WAV or M4A, at most 300 MB.

backgroundAudioUrl.description: Signed link to the background audio.

speakerName.description: Name of the speaker as it is used in the subtitles, at most 256 characters.

RenameSpeakerRequest.description: A new name for a speaker.

SyncDubbingRequest.description: The dubbing language to bring up to date.

DubbingSyncStatus.description: Whether a dubbing still matches its translation.

dubbingSubtitlesExist.description: True when the language has dubbing subtitles.

outOfSync.description: True when the translation was edited after the dubbing subtitles were made.

DubbingSegmentStatuses.description: The state of the segments of a dubbing.

segments.description: One entry per segment that is being, or was last, dubbed again.

status.description: State of the segment, for example `DONE`.

SubtitleVersion.description: An earlier saved state of a subtitle track.

savedBy.description: Who saved it. Changes made through the API are saved as `API`.

UploadUrlRequest.description: The file you are going to upload.

fileName.description: Name of the file with its extension: `mp4`, `mov`, `mp3`, `wav` or `m4a`. No path.

contentType.description: Media type of the file, for example `video/mp4` or `audio/mpeg`. Taken from the extension when left out.

recordingId.description: ID of the recording that will be made from the file. Send it back when you add the recording.

uploadUrl.description: Signed url to `PUT` the file to.

headers.description: Headers to send with the upload. They must match, or storage refuses the file.

expiresAt.description: When the url stops working, 30 minutes after it was made.

AddRecordingRequest.description: The uploaded file to add as a recording, with how to process it.

fileName.description: The `fileName` you asked the upload url for: a name with an extension and no path, at most 255 characters.

contentType.description: The `contentType` you asked the upload url for, when you sent one.

name.description: Name of the recording. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

expectedLanguages.description: Other languages that may be spoken.

subtitleProfiles.description: Subtitle profile id by language code, from `GET /v1/subtitle-profiles`.

numSpeakers.description: Number of speakers, when you know it.

ignoreTranscription.description: Keep the recording without transcribing it.

statusUrl.description: Path to poll with `GET` until the transcription is done.

CreditBalance.description: Credits your organization has left. Credits are minutes of media.

remainingMinutes.description: Minutes left. `null` when the plan has no known balance.

unlimited.description: `true` when the plan has no limit.

state.description: How the balance stands: `OK`, `WARNING` (running low), `BLOCKED` (no credits left). A blocked organization cannot start transcription, translation, dubbing or text-to-speech; reading, editing the text of subtitles and exporting still work. `null` when unknown.

action.description: `translate` is charged: every new language costs `ceil(duration / 60)` minutes. `dubbing` and `transcribe` cost `0`: `transcribe` here means transcribing a recording that exists again (retranscription). The first transcription of a file is charged when you add the recording with `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/recordings`, and cannot be estimated beforehand.

languages.description: Target languages of `translate` or `dubbing`. Not needed for `transcribe`.

reason.description: `new_language` is charged, also when you provide the subtitles of that language yourself; `already_translated` and `not_metered` cost nothing.

CostEstimate.description: The price of an action, worked out without starting it.

minutes.description: Total minutes the action would use.

enoughCredits.description: Whether the balance covers `minutes`. `null` when the balance is unknown.

allowed.description: `false` when your organization is blocked (`balance.state` is `BLOCKED`): then transcription, translation, dubbing, sync-dubbing, re-dubbing and speech are refused with `403`, whatever they cost. `true` otherwise.

pronunciationMode.description: How pronunciation is given to the engine: `inline` (IPA is written into the text), `ssml` (as phoneme markup) or `none` (not supported).

category.description: Kind of voice, set by the engine.

previewUrl.description: Link to a sample. It stops working after a day.

characteristics.description: Gender, age and use case when the engine tells them.

verifiedLanguages.description: Languages the voice is made for.

previewUrl.description: Link to a sample in this language.

TtsVoicePagination.description: Position in the list. Pass `nextPageToken` as `nextPageToken` for the next page.

nextPageToken.description: Token for the next page. Missing on the last page.

TtsVoiceFilters.description: Values you can filter voices by, for example `gender`, `age`, `useCase`. Which filters exist depends on the engine.

source.description: The word as written in the text.

notation.description: `plain` is a respelling, `ipa` is IPA. Defaults to `plain`.

text.description: Text to speak, at most 500 characters (the limit of the text-to-speech tool of Studio).

voiceId.description: Voice from `GET /v1/tts/voices` or a saved voice from `GET /v1/voices/clones`.

engine.description: Engine id from `GET /v1/tts/engines`. Defaults to `eleven_v3`. An engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

languageCode.description: Language of the text. Needed by some engines, and picks the pronunciation sets for that language.

pronunciations.description: Words to say a certain way, at most 200 together with the sets.

pronunciationIds.description: Pronunciation sets from `GET /v1/pronunciations` to apply. At most 10.

stability.description: Voice stability, from 0 to 1, where the engine has it.

similarity.description: Voice similarity, from 0 to 1, where the engine has it.

seed.description: Same seed and text give a similar result.

FavoriteVoiceRequest.description: The voice to add to the favorites of your organization.

engine.description: Engine id from `GET /v1/tts/engines`. Defaults to `eleven_v3`. An engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

Preference.description: Your default settings. New projects start with them; a project can change them for itself with `PATCH /v1/projects/{id}`.

insightsModelType.description: Provider type of the model: `GPT` for the GPT models, `CUSTOM` for `plai` and `aita`. It follows from the model.

insightsModelName.description: Model that writes summaries and insights: `gpt-5-mini` or `gpt-4o-mini`.

translationModelType.description: Provider type of the model: `GPT` for the GPT models, `CUSTOM` for `plai` and `aita`. It follows from the model.

translationModelName.description: Model that translates: `aita` (AI Translation Agent), `plai` (Phrase Language AI), `gpt-5-mini` or `gpt-4o-mini`.

mtProfileId.description: Phrase TMS machine translation profile uid. Only `plai` and `aita` use one; an empty string means none is set.

translationMemoryId.description: Phrase TMS translation memory uid. Only `plai` and `aita` use one; an empty string means none is set.

ttsProvider.description: Text-to-speech engine that new projects dub with. Some engines are switched on or off per organization: `GET /v1/tts/engines` lists the ones you can use, and an engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

UpdatePreferenceRequest.description: The default settings to change. Send only the fields that change; the others keep their value. Which of the machine translation profile and the translation memory apply depends on the translation model, as in Studio: `plai` (Phrase Language AI) takes both, chosen by you; `aita` (AI Translation Agent) takes a translation memory, and Studio chooses its machine translation profile; `gpt-5-mini` and `gpt-4o-mini` take neither. The model types follow from the models and are not sent. A field that is not a setting is ignored.

insightsModelName.description: Model that writes summaries and insights. `gpt-5-mini` or `gpt-4o-mini`.

translationModelName.description: Model that translates. `aita` is the AI Translation Agent (best quality), `plai` is Phrase Language AI, the two GPT models are the fast ones. Which of the machine translation profile and the translation memory apply depends on the translation model, as in Studio: `plai` (Phrase Language AI) takes both, chosen by you; `aita` (AI Translation Agent) takes a translation memory, and Studio chooses its machine translation profile; `gpt-5-mini` and `gpt-4o-mini` take neither. Changing the model also changes the type.

mtProfileId.description: Phrase TMS machine translation profile uid, for the translation model `plai` only. Get it from the Phrase TMS API (machine translate profiles); Studio has no endpoint that lists it. Send an empty string to remove it. For `aita` Studio chooses the profile itself (the first one of your Phrase TMS connection, or the one already set while it still exists), so do not send it; a GPT model has none. Sending it for any other model is refused with `400`.

translationMemoryId.description: Phrase TMS translation memory uid, for the translation models `plai` and `aita`. Get it from the Phrase TMS API (translation memories); Studio has no endpoint that lists it. Send an empty string to remove it. Changing to a GPT model removes it; setting it while the model is a GPT model is refused with `400`.

ttsProvider.description: Text-to-speech engine that new projects dub with. Some engines are switched on or off per organization: `GET /v1/tts/engines` lists the ones you can use, and an engine that is not available to your organization is refused with `400`.

UpdateRecordingContextRequest.description: Your correction of the video context.

contextHintUserEdited.description: Your version of `contextHint`, at most 400 characters and not blank. Tools that read the context take it instead of the detected text. Send `null` to go back to the detected one.

CulturalReview.description: The cultural review of one language: places in the video that may be sensitive for the audience of that language.

coversVisuals.description: `true` when the video pictures were reviewed too, `false` when only the text was.

flags.description: The places that may be sensitive. Empty when nothing was found.

timestamp.description: Position in the recording, in seconds.

whatWasSeen.description: What the review saw or read at that position.

whyItMayBeSensitive.description: Why it may be a problem for the audience.

languages.description: Languages to review, at most 10. Each must be a translation language of the recording.

segmentIds.description: Ids of the segments to shorten, at most 500.

dubbing.description: `true` for the dubbing track of the language.

originalText.description: The text of the segment now.

suggestedText.description: The shorter text, or `null` when no suggestion could be made (see `errorCode`).

durationSec.description: Duration of the segment, in seconds.

errorMessage.description: Details when there is no suggestion.

targetLanguage.description: Language of the track to translate again.

segmentIds.description: Ids of the segments to translate again, at most 50.

dubbing.description: `true` to translate the dubbing track of the language instead of the subtitle track.

suggestedText.description: The new translation, or `null` when none could be made (see `errorCode`).

sourceText.description: The source text that was translated.

errorMessage.description: Details when there is no suggestion.

SubtitleFileUpload.description: A subtitle file for one track.

file.description: The file: `.srt` or `.vtt`, at most 10 MB.

language.description: Language of the track the file is for.

dubbing.description: `true` to replace the dubbing track of the language.

cueSettings.description: What to do with the position settings of a `.vtt` cue (`line`, `position`, `size`, `align`, `vertical`, `region`): keep them or drop them.

imported.description: Number of subtitles that were saved.

warnings.description: Cues that were skipped, for example a cue that ends before it starts, has no duration, has no text or is shorter than 0.3 seconds.

line.description: Line of the file, `0` when it is not known.

file.description: The file: `.xlsx`, `.csv`, `.pls` or `.xml`, at most 10 MB.

PronunciationImportPreview.description: What the file contains. Nothing is saved yet.

notation.description: `plain` is the text as it is said, `ipa` is a phonetic transcription.

invalidRows.description: Rows that could not be read (at most 500 are listed).

reason.description: Why the row could not be read.

invalidRowCount.description: Number of rows that could not be read.

warnings.description: Notes about the file, for example that a sheet was ignored.

languageCode.description: Language of the file, when the file says it.

suggestedName.description: A name that is free in your organization, taken from the file name.

pairs.description: The pairs to save, usually the `pairs` of the preview, with your corrections.

notation.description: `plain` is the text as it is said, `ipa` is a phonetic transcription.

FontFile.description: One font file of a family.

id.description: File ID. Use it to download, rename or delete the file.

name.description: Label of the file inside the family.

weight.description: Weight read from the font file (400 regular, 700 bold). `null` when it is not known.

italic.description: `true` for an italic style. `null` when it is not known.

FontFamily.description: A custom font: a family with one or more files (Regular, Bold, Italic and so on).

id.description: Family ID. Use it to add styles, rename or delete the family.

fontFamily.description: The value to send as `fontFamily` in a subtitle profile, or on a single subtitle, to use this font in burned-in video: `custom:` and the family ID.

shared.description: `true` when another member of your organization uploaded the font. Everyone in the organization can use it; the uploader or an organization manager changes it.

files.description: The files of the family, by weight and then italic.
